What makes Parasaurolophus so amazing?

With a long, splendid crest on its head, the Parasaurolophus is a fascinating plant-eating dinosaur that may have made sounds with that crest.

Nature and science facts about Parasaurolophus

Parasaurolophus's crest was a hollow tube connected to its nose, so air could pass through it. According to computer simulation research, it may have used this crest to make low, trombone-like sounds. The crest was probably used to recognize others of its kind, call to mates, and communicate with the herd. It was about 9.5–10 m long and lived in North America during the Late Cretaceous.

Points worth exploring together

Point out details like the long crest (hollow tube), the trombone sound, herd communication, and walking on two or four legs. It's fun to talk about it together: "How did it make sounds with its crest?"

Parent guide — how to grow curiosity

Blow air through an empty hose or tube to make a "low sound" and imitate how the crest worked. Playing the sound of an instrument (a trombone) makes it easy to understand what the crest did.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. What did the Parasaurolophus crest do?
A. It was a hollow tube connected to its nose, so it likely made trombone-like sounds. It called to mates and communicated with the herd.

Q. Did it really make sounds with its crest?
A. Computer simulation research suggests it could have made low-pitched sounds.

Q. How can we enjoy this at home?
A. Blow air through an empty tube to make sounds, and play the sound of a trombone.
